findings.title: Project cannot be installed with `npm ci --ignore-scripts` — §5.9 gate requirement fails
findings.evidence: Iteration 3 attempted a real fix: replaced the three `@alexvegman/*` `workspace:*` devDependencies with their exact published versions ("0.1.0") and ran `npm install --package-lock-only`. That failed with `npm error code EALLOWREMOTE — Fetching packages of type "remote" have been disabled: Refusing to fetch "https://registry.npmjs.org/nyc/-/nyc-10.3.2.tgz"` — a sandbox-level restriction on this environment (registry fetch of tarballs is disabled outright; `npm view`, a metadata-only read, still works and was used for SUP-005 below), not evidence of an architectural conflict between bun workspace linking and npm resolution. The attempt was reverted: package.json restored to `workspace:*` (git checkout -- package.json), no package-lock.json was generated or committed. `bun run build` reverified clean after the revert.
findings.remediation: Retry the same exact-version-pin + `npm install --package-lock-only` attempt in an environment with real npm registry access; if it succeeds, commit the resulting package-lock.json and re-run `npm ci --ignore-scripts` + `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high` fresh. If it still fails there for a genuine architectural reason (not sandboxing), that failure mode needs to be captured and then a §11 amendment declaring the project bun-only is the correct path, per the iteration-2 report's own reasoning.

Checked @typesafe-ai/sdk@0.6.0's own type declarations (node_modules/.bun/@typesafe-ai+sdk@0.6.0/.../dist/index.d.cts) before assuming anything: `RequestOptions.signal?: AbortSignal` is real, and `systemOne(request, options?)` accepts it — so packages/decision/src/jev.ts's `JevDecisionEngine.decide` (the actual production DecisionEngine) now checks `signal?.throwIfAborted()` before starting and passes `{ signal }` into `systemOne`, covering the SDK's own internal retries (no separate retry loop exists in this file). `DecisionEngine.decide`, `EscalationEngine.explain`, and `FixProposerEngine.propose` (packages/decision/src/engine.ts, escalation.ts, fixProposer.ts) all gained an optional third `signal?: AbortSignal` parameter — optional so every existing call site and every Mock*Engine implementation keeps compiling unchanged. The three Anthropic engines named in scope (anthropicDecision.ts, anthropicEscalation.ts, anthropicFixProposer.ts) each check `signal?.throwIfAborted()` before their one `fetch` call and pass `signal` into that `fetch` call directly — `fetch`'s native `AbortSignal` support means this is real mid-flight cancellation, not just a pre-flight check, for the honest reason these files make exactly one attempt each (no retry loop to check between). Tests added: anthropicDecision.test.ts, anthropicEscalation.test.ts, anthropicFixProposer.test.ts each gained a test constructing the engine with an already-aborted AbortController signal, spying on global fetch, and asserting the call rejects AND fetch was never invoked. Verified capable of failing: temporarily removed the `throwIfAborted()` guard from anthropicDecision.ts, reran that file's API-009 test — it failed (`expect(fetchSpy).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` — fetch WAS called, since without the guard the aborted signal still reaches `fetch`, which itself throws asynchronously after being "called"), confirming the assertion covers the actual defect and isn't a false-positive pass. Restored and reran green.
